Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Bangladeshi players are out in the huddle and both the umpires walk out, followed by the Kiwi openers Will Young and Rachin Ravindra as they take the crease. Shoriful Islam the left-handed quicky will bowl the first over for the visitors.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Bangladesh performed decently, recovering from early setbacks. As their innings conclude, their bowlers will now be eager to pick early wickets in the powerplay and put the hosts on the back foot. On the other hand, New Zealand will aim to seal the series with another comprehensive batting performance. Time will tell. Stay tuned for an action-packed run chase.

New Zealand, having started well by removing Anamul, Shanto, and Litton Das early on, struggled to capitalize in the middle overs. Jacob Duffy completed a three-wicket haul, including the crucial dismissal of Rahim, while Adam Milne chipped in with a wicket. Despite the spinners maintaining economy in the middle overs, they couldn't create enough opportunities to pressurize the visitors in the middle overs and the ones they created, they were not able to capitalize on with Rachin Ravindra also dropping Soumya Sarkar which could have made a big impact on the total. Adithya Ashok and Josh Clarkson, got their maiden ODI wickets with O'Rourke, plucking his first three scalps in the last over of the innings. New Zealand managed to keep Bangladesh below 300.

Take a bow, Soumya Sarkar! What a sensational knock that was and he also breaks Sachin Tendulkar's record of the highest individual score by a sub-continent batter in New Zealand. The Bangladeshi innings has come to a close after New Zealand invited them to bat first at the picturesque Saxton Oval Stadium. The visitors faced an uphill challenge right in the beginning, as they lost Anamul Haque in the fifth over, followed by the quick dismissals of skipper Shanto and Litton Das. However, Soumya Sarkar looked completely unbothered throughout. He provided a glimmer of hope for his team with his confident and noteworthy century scoring 169 runs, forming a resilient partnership of 91 runs with the experienced Mushfiqur Rahim. The duo held their ground in the middle overs, contributing significantly before Mushfiqur was dismissed after a well-made 45. Mehidy Hasan Miraz followed up nicely with his contribution. He, too, stitched up a 50-run stand with Soumya Sarkar. Bangladesh managed to score a tough total of 291 runs with some handy cameos down the order.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start! The New Zealand players walk out to the field so do the Bangladeshi openers and we are just moments away from the first ball. Adam Milne to open the bowling for the hosts. Soumya Sarkar and Anamul Haque to open for the visitors.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Soumya Sarkar, Anamul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Litton Das, Towhid Hridoy, Mushfiqur Rahim (WK), Mehidy Hasan, Shoriful Islam, Rishad Hossain (In place of Afif Hossain & On Debut), Tanzim Hasan Sakib (In place of Mustafizur Rahman), Hasan Mahmud.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Will Young, Rachin Ravindra, Henry Nicholls, Tom Latham (C), Tom Blundell (WK), Mark Chapman, Josh Clarkson, Adam Milne, Adithya Ashok (In place of Ish Sodhi & On Debut), Jacob Duffy, William O'Rourke.
TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

On the other hand, Bangladesh will have to put up some loads if they want to sustain in this 3-match ODI series. From their bowling department, only Shoriful Islam was able to get a couple of wickets at the start of the match, but as they were able to take the wheels out of the Kiwis, the Tigers could not break the partnership which created havoc for their batting unit at the time of chasing. It was although not at all a terrible inning for Bangladesh, as the batting unit did their part, but a bit more runs from Soumya Sarkar and Mushfiqur Rahim would help the team challenge the Kiwis. The bowling lineup will also need to correct their lines and lengths, to get rid of the extras they had put in the first match. But will the Tigers roar back again at the Kiwis? Let's find out. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned!

New Zealand is in the front seat, having control of the ODI series as they won the first match of the despite resting a few first-team players. All credit to Will Young for his impactful century and captain Tom Latham's strong 92-run knock, which enabled the Kiwis to win the opening One-Day International by 44 runs. If the Kiwis win this match, they will be continuing their domination of the Head-to-Head since 2021. The bowling department of the Black Caps was superlative, as the attack of Adam Milne, Ish Sodhi, and Josh Clarkson graved the Tiger's batting lineup by taking 6 wickets altogether. The only drawback from the first match of the Black Caps was the batting lineup, as the other batters except Will Young and Tom Latham will need to buckle up to stretch more for this game.
